challenge.web.label: Scenario · Web portal
challenge.web.title: Suspicious portal traffic
challenge.web.brief: The WAF detects unusual requests against a public portal. Investigate the most heavily reported source and correlate WAF and application logs: the ticket specifies which request to analyze.
challenge.web.hint: Compare IPs and reputation, then follow the request ID for /admin through the WAF and application logs. Reputation alone does not prove compromise.
challenge.web.success: Case solved. IP 203.0.113.77 has numerous reports and generated SQL injection and path traversal attempts blocked by the WAF. Request w103 to /admin reached the application, which returned 404. The available logs do not confirm compromise, but do not rule it out: host and database checks are still needed. Document the evidence, continue investigating and consider containment according to procedure.
challenge.mail.label: Scenario · Email security
challenge.mail.title: An urgent invoice
challenge.mail.brief: An employee reports an email that appears to come from a supplier. Analyze the message, authentication results, link and gateway action.
challenge.mail.hint: Compare the link domain with the visible sender. An SPF pass for the envelope domain does not automatically mean DMARC passes for the visible sender.
challenge.mail.success: Case solved. The link points to login.billing-update.example and the message fails DMARC: SPF passes for an unaligned domain and DKIM fails. The gateway quarantined m-481. The evidence neither confirms nor rules out credential entry: click data and recipient confirmation are missing. Document the case, check for other recipients and consider containment according to procedure.
challenge.formInstructions: Explore the evidence in the terminal and complete the report below. Switching scenarios resets the current case.
challenge.actionsInstructions: Select all actions appropriate for this case.
challenge.action.document: Document events, indicators and evidence in the ticket.
challenge.action.investigate: Investigate missing evidence and involve the relevant teams.
challenge.action.contain: Consider appropriate containment according to procedure.
challenge.action.dismiss: Close the case immediately without further checks.
challenge.feedbackTitle: Review these points and try again:
challenge.feedback.ip: Check the reputation and source specified in the ticket.
challenge.feedback.attacks: Review the attack categories associated with the identified source.
challenge.feedback.request: Correlate the /admin request across WAF and application logs.
challenge.feedback.http: Check the application response for that request.
challenge.feedback.domain: Check the exact domain of the link in the message.
challenge.feedback.dmarc: Review the DMARC result and sender alignment.
challenge.feedback.delivery: Check the gateway action for the specified message.
challenge.feedback.outcome: Distinguish what the evidence confirms from what remains unknown.
challenge.feedback.actions: Reconsider documentation, investigation and containment before closing.
challenge.title: A shift in the SOC
challenge.intro: Choose a simulated case, explore the evidence and reconstruct events like a SOC analyst.
challenge.brief: The WAF detects unusual requests against a public portal. Investigate the most heavily reported source, distinguish its traffic from other activity, and correlate WAF events with application logs.
challenge.questionIp: What is the suspicious source IP?
challenge.questionAttacks: Which two attack categories are associated with that IP?
challenge.questionRequest: What is the request ID for the /admin request that reached the application?
challenge.questionStatus: What HTTP status did the application return for that request?
challenge.questionOutcome: Is a compromise confirmed by the available evidence?
challenge.answerGuideAttacks: Choose two codes from: sqli, traversal, xss, rce. The order does not matter.
challenge.answerGuideOutcome: For the outcome, use confirmed or unconfirmed.
challenge.note: Simulated scenario and data. Use help to see the available commands; the buttons open logs quickly.
challenge.welcome: Analyst console ready. Type help or use the buttons below.
challenge.result.help:
Available commands:
ls — list evidence
cat <file> — show a file
grep <word> <file> — filter lines
hint — get a clue
clear — clear the terminal

Use the report below the terminal to submit your answers.
challenge.result.hint: Compare IPs against the baseline and threat intelligence. Check WAF rules and actions; use request IDs to compare forwarded requests with origin.log. A 404 or a negative reputation does not prove a compromise.
challenge.result.notFound: File not found. Use ls to see the available evidence.
challenge.result.submitUsage: Format: submit <ip> <attack1> <attack2> <request-id> <http> <outcome>. Type help for accepted codes.
challenge.result.incorrect: That answer is not correct. Review the timeline and try again, or use hint.
challenge.result.success: Case solved. IP 203.0.113.77 has numerous reports and attempted SQL injection and path traversal; the WAF blocked the corresponding requests with 403 responses. Request w103 to /admin was forwarded and the application returned 404; /robots.txt also returned 404. The XSS event came from another IP. The available evidence does not confirm compromise, but does not rule it out: database audit and host investigation are among the missing evidence. Document the events, consider blocking the source according to procedure, and continue investigating and monitoring.

buildweeks.buildweek-1.title: Secure network & Python tools
buildweeks.buildweek-1.description: Team leader for a segmented business network project covering 120 hosts, with three Python tools to analyse HTTP services, TCP ports and network traffic.
buildweeks.buildweek-1.overview: I served as team leader for the Build Week project about the fictional Theta company. The team project combines a six-floor network, DMZ services and analysis tools. The collection includes the Packet Tracer topology, configuration report, cost estimate, slides, three documented scripts and lab logs.
buildweeks.buildweek-1.activity.0: Segmentation with six VLANs, 802.1Q trunks, inter-VLAN routing and DHCP addressing.
buildweeks.buildweek-1.activity.1: Definition of ACLs, firewall zones, NAS access and DMZ web server isolation.
buildweeks.buildweek-1.activity.2: HTTP method analysis, TCP scanning and IPv4 traffic inspection with Python raw sockets.
buildweeks.buildweek-1.activity.3: Log collection and technical documentation of network design decisions and test results.
buildweeks.buildweek-2.title: Black-box challenges & penetration testing
buildweeks.buildweek-2.description: From the Harry Potter-themed HogTheta challenge to Jangow01 and LupinOne: clues, enumeration and privilege escalation, alongside assessments and testing of web applications and services.
buildweeks.buildweek-2.overview: Black-box challenges are at the heart of this Build Week: analysing lab machines without prior information, connecting clues and reconstructing the path to privileged access. HogTheta brings the investigation into the world of Harry Potter; Jangow01 and LupinOne explore application vulnerabilities, exposed credentials and insecure configurations. The nine documents also cover SQL Injection and XSS in DVWA, Samba and Tomcat assessments, and C code analysis.
buildweeks.buildweek-2.activity.0: Testing SQL Injection and Stored XSS in DVWA, with request analysis using Burp Suite.
buildweeks.buildweek-2.activity.1: Nmap reconnaissance, Nessus vulnerability assessment and lab validation with Metasploit.
buildweeks.buildweek-2.activity.2: The Harry Potter-themed HogTheta, Jangow01 and LupinOne challenges: enumeration, clue analysis and privilege escalation in the lab.
buildweeks.buildweek-2.activity.3: Analysis of C program behaviour, input bounds and buffer overflow cases.

buildweeks.challenge.hogtheta.title: HogTheta · Harry Potter
buildweeks.challenge.hogtheta.descriptio: A Harry Potter-themed investigation involving hidden clues, steganography, SQL Injection and port knocking. Two documents describe the paths explored by the team to gain root access: a technical report and the “Chronicles of HogTheta”.
buildweeks.challenge.jangow.title: Jangow01 · From reconnaissance to root
buildweeks.challenge.jangow.description: Reconnaissance and enumeration, discovery of exposed credentials and an RCE vulnerability, followed by analysis of an outdated kernel for privilege escalation.
buildweeks.challenge.lupin.title: LupinOne · Clues and insecure configurations
buildweeks.challenge.lupin.description: Web enumeration and directory fuzzing, recovery of an SSH key, and analysis of insecure permissions and sudo configuration. The report reconstructs the chain of weaknesses leading to root privileges.
